value.body: A bookkeeper keeps the day-to-day records of a business: sales, purchases, payments, receipts and petty cash. Employers include small businesses, shops, traders, CA firms and accounting outsourcing centres. A typical day involves entering vouchers and invoices, matching them with bank statements, and keeping records ready for the accountant.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com or BBA; Class 12 with a Tally course for some roles

items.label: Reports to
items.value: An accountant or the business owner

items.note: All years of the course; B.Com is one common entry degree for bookkeeping

items.note: Cumulative registrations since July 2020; counts enterprises, not bookkeeping jobs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start in small firms or CA offices after a short practical course in Tally, GST and basic accounting. Part-time and remote bookkeeping for several small businesses is also common.

value.title: At a glance
items: Often a starting point for an accountant career.
Routine entry work is increasingly automated by accounting software.

value.note: Regular mode only (distance mode excluded); rounded to one decimal. Counts all years of the course, not graduates.
